intro.title: useClickOutside
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useClickOutside` that detects when a user clicks outside a specific element, a common pattern for closing modals, dropdowns, or popups. You'll learn how to use the `useEffect` hook to add and clean up event listeners, and how to manage references to DOM elements with the `useRef` hook. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the native JavaScript `addEventListener` method for handling click events. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that improves user interface interactions in your applications.
intro.usecase: The useClickOutside hook is essential for creating intuitive UI components that respond to user interaction outside their boundaries. You'll find this pattern in dropdown menus that close when clicking elsewhere, modal dialogs that dismiss when clicking the backdrop, and floating tooltips that disappear when users interact with other page elements. In dashboards, it's used for collapsible filter panels that close when selections are made elsewhere, and in forms for date pickers that close after date selection. This pattern improves UX by reducing visual clutter and preventing overlapping interactive elements.
